title: JM Fleet Lathe CAM Operation Template Matrix
family_count_note: v1.1 (2026-06-01) expanded 8 -> 15 families per the corpus matrix-expansion blueprint (CAM-CORPUS-PROGRAMMING-NOTES.md sec.5): added profile, face_grooving (split from radial grooving), chamfer, bore_finish, live_tool_milling, peck_drill, tap(stub). Covers the Fusion turning op-type set toward 'a CAM operation for ALL operations in Fusion'.
goal_directive: plot out best ways to generate a CAM operation for ALL operations in Fusion; templates for every toolpath type with variable params + cutting conditions; JM-fleet-focused; learn from prior programs' inefficiencies and optimize for time+efficiency+safety+accuracy; write against JM-purchased tools.
grounding: 8 family analyses from workflow worka68bp (REAL observed JM .MIN cutting conditions + inefficiencies) + kilo CAM/lathe domain expertise + JM tool sources. Optimize/template workflow phases hit StructuredOutput flake; synthesized here by the domain owner.
machine_fleet: LTH-01..07 Okuma OSP (100% Okuma G-mode lathes at JM Die)

okuma_mode_legend._dialect_note: Okuma OSP dialect — INVERTED vs Fanuc. CORRECTED 2026-06-01 from 16,558-program corpus evidence (CAM-CORPUS-PROGRAMMING-NOTES.md). A Fanuc-trained reading (G71=rough/G70=finish/G75=groove/G76=thread) mis-classifies the ENTIRE JM corpus. Fanuc G70/G72-face/G73/G75/G33 are absent (~0 each).
okuma_mode_legend.G94: feed = in/min — direct feed-per-minute (rare; live-tool C/Y-axis blocks only, ~6-8%, reverts to G95 after)
okuma_mode_legend.G95: feed = in/REV — feed-per-REVOLUTION. OSP IMPLICIT MODAL DEFAULT (stated in only ~9-10% of files; ~91% omit it and rely on the per-rev default). Misreading as /min is a 12-60x feed error. CONFIRMS U-CAM-FEEDREV-MODE-DEFAULT.
okuma_mode_legend.G96: constant surface speed (S = SFM, not rpm) — spindle modulates to hold surface speed (~92% of files)
okuma_mode_legend.G97: direct rpm (S = rpm) — used for on-center drill/bore/thread (~95%)
okuma_mode_legend.G50: max-rpm cap under G96 — MUST be set whenever G96 active (safety invariant; ~97-98% compliance observed, ~1.9% uncapped = highest-severity gap)
okuma_mode_legend.G85: LAP ROUGH cycle (D=DOC, U=X-stock, W=Z-stock, F=feed) — the workhorse rougher, ~73% of files
okuma_mode_legend.G87: LAP FINISH cycle — replays the SAME named G81/G82 shape at finish stock (zero geometry re-code), ~69%
okuma_mode_legend.G80: LAP END (closes a G81/G82 shape block) — ~73%
okuma_mode_legend.G71: THREADING cycle (B=angle, D=depth/pass, U=finish-stock, H=height, J=lead/TPI, M33/M73) — ~3%, runs under G97
okuma_mode_legend.G72: THREADING cycle (transverse/face thread variant) — pairs with G71
okuma_mode_legend.G74: peck-drill / peck-groove cycle (X0 Z-depth D=peck L=retract F)
okuma_mode_legend.G76: corner CHAMFER/RADIUS inside a LAP shape (A=angle, L=radius) — NOT threading; ~5-7%
okuma_mode_legend.G41_G42_G40: tool-nose-radius (TNR) comp on / on / off — finish-pass only, ~21% (so ~79% cut on programmed-point geometry — accuracy opportunity)
okuma_mode_legend.A_angle: chamfer shorthand (G1 X.. A135/A225) instead of explicit chamfer coords — ~59%
okuma_mode_legend._G75_correction: Fanuc G75 grooving is ABSENT in the JM Okuma corpus (~0). Earlier matrix/rules versions WRONGLY assumed 'Okuma G75 auto-depth grooving' — that was Fanuc contamination, corrected here. Real JM grooving = single-plunge (frequently, often poorly) OR G74 peck-groove OR G81/G82 LAP define+replay (face-groove done well via G85/G82+G41 -> G87).

physics_delegation.rule: NEVER inline Kienzle/Taylor/material/SFM constants. Cutting numbers are COMPUTED at generation time via the physics surfaces below; templates carry only the RULE + the driver inputs. observed_baseline numbers are HISTORICAL DATA records (allowed), NOT constants to reuse as recommendations.
physics_delegation.speed_feed: prism_calc speed/feed actions + UltimateSpeedFeedEngine (SFC) — input {material ISO group, tool grade, op family, diameter, DOC} → {SFM, feed, rpm} with confidence
physics_delegation.lathe_physics_safety: whiskey prism_turning (373 actions) + prism_thread (22) — lathe_safety_predicate_evaluate, lathe_partoff_safety_gate, G50/CSS, L/D deflection

tool_sources.primary: ShopToolLibraryEngine.ts — authoritative JM shop-proven production tools w/ proven cutting params. Loads 7 shop-tools-*.csv (turning/endmill/boring-rough/boring-finish/insert-drills-130/insert-drills-180/twist-drills). NOTE: CSV files NOT YET ON DISK — ingest is a prerequisite for tool-aware generation (build step #7).
tool_sources.vendor_catalogs: Tungaloy (2,973 inserts: 2,561 turning + 323 threading + 89 grooving) + Widia (1,122) — ISO-classified insert geometry/grade, used when ShopToolLibrary lacks a match.
tool_sources.selector: jmDieSelectorCatalog.ts — JM tool package/holder inventory tied to Fusion 360 exports (the customer-availability binding the operator asked for).
tool_sources.tool_folders_status: H:/PRISM/JM DIE/{TOOL HOLDERS,TOOLING,MATERIALS} are EMPTY on disk — physical-inventory ingest pending (charlie/hotel own purchase data).
tool_sources.observed_tcode_families: T01/T12=OD rough turn (CNMG-432, .032R), T02=OD finish (.015R), T03/T05=center/spot drill, T06=thread chaser/tool, T07/T08/T09=ID boring bar, T10=face groove finish, T11=parting (1/8 carbide insert, fleet-universal across 16,558 .MIN)

global_safety_invariants: G50 max-rpm cap MUST be emitted whenever G96 is active (no uncapped CSS — small ID would over-speed).
Boring-bar L/D <= 4 for steel, <= 6 for carbide-shanked — else deflection/chatter; escalate to whiskey lathe_safety_predicate_evaluate.

Parting/grooving: if groove/cutoff depth > 3x insert width -> MUST peck (Okuma G74 peck-and-shift, or G81/G82 LAP define+replay for profiled/face grooves); no single full-depth plunge. NOT Fanuc G75 (absent in JM Okuma corpus).
Threading: respect min/max pitch DOC; multi-pass infeed; no full-depth single pass.
Every generated op runs prism_safety:validate_physics shop_floor gate (Omega>=0.95, S(x)>=0.98) BEFORE Fusion drive / post.
INCH everywhere (JM imperial); never assume mm; G95 feeds are in/REV not in/min.

template_field_contract.fusion_strategy: best-known Fusion adsk.cam turning operation type — VERIFY against live add-in /post + CAM-template nav before the generator binds it (fusion_strategy_verified=false until live-checked).
template_field_contract.observed_baseline: REAL JM cutting conditions from worka68bp analyses — historical record + the thing we optimize AGAINST.
template_field_contract.fixed_params: Fusion op params that do not vary by part.
template_field_contract.variable_params: params driven by {material, diameter, tool, finish, depth} — each names its DRIVER + SOURCE.
template_field_contract.cutting_condition_rule: how SFM/feed/DOC are COMPUTED (physics-delegated) — never inline.
template_field_contract.optimizations_over_baseline: the inefficiencies to beat (from analyses) + the optimal approach.

facing.applies_when: Stock face cleanup / Z-datum establishment / OD or ID face finishing before/after turning.

observed_baseline.strategy: Direct linear facing: G0 rapid to start Z, G1 linear feed to center. Most common pattern.
observed_baseline.sfm: 200-250 (G96 CSS) for rough; RPM 600-1000 (G97) when direct
observed_baseline.feed: 0.005-0.010 in/rev (G95) — units ambiguous in some direct G1 blocks

variable_params.name: facing_passes
variable_params.rule: single pass if <= max_rough_DOC else N = ceil(stock/DOC); finish pass always separate

variable_params.name: min_diameter_for_css
variable_params.rule: below this dia, CSS would exceed G50 -> spindle holds capped rpm

facing.cutting_condition_rule: G96 CSS rough+finish; SFM/feed/DOC from prism_calc speed/feed for {ISO group, grade, 'facing', face_dia}. Finish: lighter feed scaled to nose radius for surface finish (accuracy goal).
optimizations_over_baseline: KILL multi-pass air-cutting: baseline does 3-5 G0/Z-offset passes where 1-2 higher-DOC passes hold (DIEBUTTONS.MIN repeats Z-offset contour 3x = redundant rapids). Compute true pass count from stock, not a fixed 3.
Use G96 CSS not fixed G97 so cutting speed stays constant as tool approaches center (better finish + faster).
Single rough + single finish split — no redundant intermediate passes.
safety_gates: finish DOC >= insert min-chip-load to avoid rubbing

OD_roughing.applies_when: External-diameter stock removal to near-net before finish.

observed_baseline.strategy: Okuma G85 NTURN / G87 repeat-pass; manual 3-pass G0/G1 setup; G96 S250-550 SFM, G50 cap S600-800; G95 feed 0.005-0.007 in/rev (up to 0.009); DOC 0.031-0.040 in radial; nominal 3 passes (often 2 redundant air-cuts).

fixed_params.cycle: Fusion roughing (auto-generates passes) — replaces manual G85 coding

variable_params.name: max_roughing_stepdown (radial DOC)
variable_params.note: raise toward 0.060-0.100 in where rigidity allows (baseline 0.031-0.040 is conservative)

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: modern carbide steel 600-1000+ SFM vs baseline 250 — large headroom

variable_params.name: g50_cap_rpm
variable_params.driver: max safe rpm for largest chuck/part

OD_roughing.cutting_condition_rule: G96 CSS; let Fusion roughing compute pass count from stock model (NEVER hand-code redundant passes). SFM/feed/DOC from physics; cap rpm via G50.
optimizations_over_baseline: Eliminate redundant air-cutting passes (15-30 s/part): baseline manually codes 3 G1 passes at same Z then calls cycle — only pass 1 cuts, 2-3 cut air. Fusion stock-aware roughing removes this entirely.
Raise SFM off conservative 250 toward physics envelope for the grade/material (time goal).
Increase radial DOC where machine rigidity + L/D allow — fewer passes (MRR / efficiency goal).

OD_finishing.applies_when: Final OD pass to tolerance + surface finish after roughing.

observed_baseline.strategy: Paired rough-then-finish in all examined programs. Finish: G96 (450-650 SFM observed), single profile pass, finish insert .015R.
observed_baseline.feed: lighter than rough (0.003-0.006 in/rev typical for finish)
observed_baseline.note: G50 cap 600-800 forces sub-surface cutting on larger diameters

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: headroom to 800-1200 SFM modern carbide steel

variable_params.name: finish_feed_per_rev
variable_params.rule: feed scaled so theoretical Ra = f^2/(8*nose_R) meets print finish — ACCURACY goal

OD_finishing.cutting_condition_rule: G96 CSS; finish feed derived from surface-finish requirement (Ra = f^2/(8*R)) — accuracy-first; SFM from physics for tool life.
optimizations_over_baseline: Raise conservative finish SFM (450-650) toward modern-carbide envelope where tool life allows.
Re-evaluate low G50 cap — only cap for genuine chuck/part-balance limits, not defensive habit (baseline leaves 200-300 rpm margin).
Feed chosen from finish-requirement physics, not copied 0.006 default.
safety_gates: feed not below insert min-chip-load (rubbing -> poor finish + heat)

ID_boring.applies_when: Enlarge/finish a drilled/cored hole to ID tolerance.

observed_baseline.strategy: Two-op: NAT07 rough/semi-finish bar + NAT08 finish bar. Okuma G97 FIXED rpm 650-780; G1 Z plunge to depth in 1-2 passes.

fixed_params.retract: along axis, no scrape on exit

variable_params.name: bar_overhang_LD
variable_params.rule: L/D <= 4 steel, <= 6 carbide; if exceeded -> derate SFM/feed or escalate whiskey deflection

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: headroom to 200+ SFM modern carbide vs baseline 50-75

variable_params.name: use_css
variable_params.rule: G96 if dia variation warrants; else G97 — baseline locked G97 unnecessarily

ID_boring.cutting_condition_rule: SFM from physics (raise off 50-75 where L/D permits); feed derated by deflection model (whiskey); G96 CSS where bore dia varies, else G97.

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: carbide boring bar (3/16-1/2 shank), .015R finish insert; 21 bar types by L/D
jm_tool_mapping.source: ShopToolLibrary boring-rough.csv + boring-finish.csv | Tungaloy ID turning

optimizations_over_baseline: Raise SFM/RPM off 50-75 SFM toward modern carbide 200+ where L/D allows (huge time waste at baseline).
Feed 0.0015 -> 0.003-0.005 in/rev where deflection model permits.
Use G96 CSS for adaptive speed instead of hardcoded G97 (baseline locked fixed rpm).
L/D-aware bar selection from ShopToolLibrary (pick shortest bar that reaches depth).
safety_gates: chip evacuation on deep bore (peck/retract if needed)

drilling_centering.applies_when: Center/spot then through/blind axial hole on centerline.

observed_baseline.strategy: Two-op: (1) center drill manual peck via G1 Z-retract, 0.1-0.15 in deep, 600-800 rpm G97, F 0.001-0.002 in/rev; (2) peck drill G74 cycle, F 0.001-0.002, peck D 0.15-0.3 in.
observed_baseline.note: 0.14 in and 0.375 in drills run near-identical speeds despite 2.7x dia ratio

fixed_params.cycle: Fusion drilling (maps to Okuma G74 peck on post)

variable_params.name: peck_depth
variable_params.rule: deep-hole peck scaled to dia, not fixed 0.15-0.2

variable_params.name: rpm
variable_params.note: MUST scale with dia — baseline runs all drills same rpm

variable_params.name: spot_depth
variable_params.rule: enough to guide + chamfer, not over-deep

drilling_centering.cutting_condition_rule: rpm = SFM*12/(pi*dia) per-drill (G97 for drilling); feed/rev + peck from physics for {dia, depth, material}; spot depth from point geometry.

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: center/spot drill 120-135deg; jobber/insert drill (130 or 180 point)

optimizations_over_baseline: Scale rpm WITH drill dia (baseline runs 0.14 in and 0.375 in at same rpm = 10-25% time waste on big drills).
Peck depth proportional to dia + chip-breaking need, not fixed 0.15 (baseline 12-15 pecks on deep holes wastes 2-3 s/hole on dwell).
Insert drills for >0.5 in where ShopToolLibrary has them (faster than jobber).

observed_baseline.strategy: 3 patterns: (1) manual multi-pass G0/G1 (FEED ROLL GROOVE.MIN = 41 manual blocks!); (2) boring-bar groove cycle; (3) face groove. G97 fixed (~S300), SFM ~70 inferred.
observed_baseline.tools: T09/T10 face groove (.0156R/.0078R), T11 cutoff/parting blade

fixed_params.cycle: Fusion groove -> Okuma G74 peck-groove (X.. Z-d D<peck> L<retract> F) for radial grooves, OR G81/G82 LAP define+replay for profiled/face grooves. NOT G75 (Fanuc — ABSENT in JM corpus, dialect correction 2026-06-01). Replaces the 41 hand-coded G0/G1 blocks + single-deep-plunge+G4-dwell habit observed.

variable_params.name: peck_step
variable_params.rule: if depth > 3x width -> peck-and-shift (G74 peck-groove); step from physics

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: raise off ~70 SFM where rigidity allows

variable_params.name: width_passes
variable_params.rule: multi-plunge step-over for wide grooves

grooving.cutting_condition_rule: G74 peck-and-shift (radial) or G81/G82 LAP (profile/face groove); SFM/feed from physics for grooving op; depth-vs-width 3x peck rule enforced.
optimizations_over_baseline: Replace 41 manual G0/G1 blocks (FEED ROLL GROOVE.MIN) + the single-deep-plunge+G4-dwell habit with a G74 peck-and-shift cycle (radial) or G81/G82 LAP (profile/face) — fewer lines, no Z-offset typo propagation. NOT Fanuc G75 (absent in JM Okuma corpus).
Auto peck-stepping from physics, not hand-coded depths.
Raise SFM off ~70 where groove dia + rigidity allow.
Add a side+bottom spring/finish pass on dimensional (snap-ring/seal) grooves — baseline single plunge will not hold size.

observed_baseline.strategy: All 6 samples identical: T11 dedicated carbide parting insert (fleet standard across all 16,558 .MIN); G96 S100-250 SFM + G50 cap S600-800; G95 feed 0.0015-0.005 in/rev; actual rpm 150-600 on 0.75-1.5 in OD.
observed_baseline.note: G96 S250 + redundant G50 S600 = defensive double-limit, 15-25% spindle waste on small OD

fixed_params.approach: to center (or slightly past for full sever)

variable_params.name: feed_per_rev
variable_params.note: lighter near center to avoid burr/grab

variable_params.name: peck
variable_params.rule: peck for chip evac on large dia; retract reduces re-cut

variable_params.name: css_ramp_at_center
variable_params.rule: G96 would spike rpm at center -> G50 cap protects; consider feed taper

parting_cutoff.cutting_condition_rule: G96 CSS + mandatory G50 cap; feed from physics, taper near center; peck for deep cutoff.
optimizations_over_baseline: Trim defensive double-limit (G96 S250 + G50 S600 leaves margin) — set G50 only at true safe-max (15-25% spindle utilization reclaimed on small OD).
Reduce multi-pass air-cut rapids between passes (30-50% of cutoff cycle is positioning on baseline 0.2 in cutoff).
Feed taper toward center to control burr (accuracy) without stalling.
safety_gates: G50 cap MANDATORY (CSS spikes rpm as dia->0)

observed_baseline.strategy: Okuma G71 rapid stock-removal threading cycle. T06 thread tool always. G97 direct rpm (no G96 observed). FIXED DOC 0.003 in/pass across ALL pitches.

variable_params.name: thread_doc_per_pass
variable_params.rule: ADAPT 0.001-0.010 by pitch (NOT fixed 0.003); decreasing-DOC infeed for constant chip area

variable_params.name: rpm/sfm
variable_params.rule: pitch-dependent rpm or G96 CSS (baseline constant 250-300 makes SFM vary 25-123 across diameters)

variable_params.name: thread_spec
variable_params.source: thread tables (UN/metric/NPT) — pitch, depth, major/minor/pitch dia

threading.cutting_condition_rule: G71 multi-pass; DOC schedule adapts to pitch (decreasing-DOC for constant chip area); rpm pitch/dia-aware or G96; spec from thread tables.
optimizations_over_baseline: Adapt DOC to pitch (baseline fixed 0.003 wastes 30-50% on coarse 4.5 TPI, risks chatter on fine 32 TPI).
Decreasing-DOC infeed schedule (constant chip area) instead of equal-DOC.
Pitch/dia-aware rpm or G96 CSS (baseline constant 250-300 -> SFM 25-123 swing).
CSS ramp-down at thread end (baseline has none).
safety_gates: spindle-sync feed lock (threading feed = pitch, not overridable)

profile.applies_when: General multi-arc/multi-segment OD or ID contour (electrodes, lobed forms, stepped profiles) — the corpus's LARGEST hand-coded class (CSM 6-lobe, OMG punch-holder, profiler NAT09/NAT10, FONTANA B-8740).

observed_baseline.strategy: Frequently HAND-CODED line-by-line G1/G2/G3 stepover (extremes 1120-2516 lines, ~140-line profilers) OR posted CAM with 14-25 stepped passes and no CSS. Best-practice minority uses G85 N<shape>/G81(G82)/G80 LAP define + G87 finish replay.
observed_baseline.note: ~27% of corpus has NO LAP at all — most of that longhand lives in this family.

fixed_params.cycle: Fusion profile -> Okuma G85 N<shape> D/U/W/F (LAP rough) over a G81 (longitudinal) or G82 (face) shape-def + G80; G87 N<shape> finish replay (zero geometry re-code). NOT longhand G1/G2/G3.
fixed_params.compensation: TNR comp (G41/G42) on the G87 finish over arcs/angles

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: G96 CSS so surface speed holds across the varying contour diameter

profile.cutting_condition_rule: G96 CSS over the contour (G50 capped); LAP define+replay computes passes from the shape, never hand-stepped. SFM/feed/DOC physics-delegated per {ISO, grade, profile, local dia}.

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: OD/ID profiling insert (CNMG/DNMG/VNMG by access angle)

optimizations_over_baseline: Promote hand-coded G1/G2/G3 contours (1120-2516 line extremes) to a G85/G81-G82/G80 LAP define + G87 replay — orders-of-magnitude less code, controller-optimized passes, no typo propagation.
Force G96 CSS over the contour (posted profilers run fixed G97 -> speed collapses on small-dia segments).
Single shape-def, replayed at finish via G87 (no doubled geometry / rough-finish drift).
safety_gates: L/D radial-deflection gate on slender contours (whiskey)
TNR comp on formed finish for arc/taper accuracy

face_grooving.applies_when: Face/transverse groove or recess (seal/relief/pocket on the part face) — DISTINCT from radial grooving. JM does this WELL via G82 LAP (ITW 5605, AGRATI A9087329, ATF T2790, EJOT, TCR, CHOCTAW).

observed_baseline.strategy: G85 N<shape>/G82 (face/transverse shape-def) + G41 rough -> G87 finish replay. A genuine shop strength.

fixed_params.cycle: Fusion face-groove -> Okuma G82 face shape-def under G85 LAP rough + G87 finish; G74 peck-and-shift on depth where depth>3x width.

variable_params.name: peck_step
variable_params.rule: depth > 3x width -> peck-and-shift (G74); step from physics

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: face-groove dia SWEEPS as the tool moves radially -> G96 over-speeds at small dia, G50 cap mandatory

face_grooving.cutting_condition_rule: G82 LAP define + G87 replay; SFM/feed physics-delegated (grooving op); depth-vs-width 3x peck enforced; G50 cap because face-groove dia sweeps under G96.
optimizations_over_baseline: Promote this strong G82-LAP idiom as the DEFAULT for face grooves (vs single-plunge); preserve as positive training signal (R11).
Add side+bottom spring/finish pass on dimensional (seal) grooves.
G50 cap mandatory under G96 because the face-groove diameter sweeps toward center.
safety_gates: G50 cap MANDATORY under G96 (sweeping dia)

chamfer.applies_when: Edge break / lead-in chamfer / part-face break — appears in ~59% of corpus files as A-angle shorthand or G76 in-shape corner.

observed_baseline.strategy: G1 X.. A135/A225 angle shorthand, or G76 X.. A<angle> L<radius> corner inside a LAP shape, or G3 corner on the part face at cutoff.
observed_baseline.note: Okuma G76 here = corner chamfer/radius, NOT threading.

fixed_params.cycle: Okuma A-angle shorthand (G1 X.. A<deg>) or G76 X.. A<angle> L<radius> in-shape corner — NOT a separate roughing cycle.

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: rides the finish-pass CSS; G50 capped

chamfer.cutting_condition_rule: emit as A-angle/G76 corner on the finish pass; SFM/feed inherit the finish CSS (G50 capped); size from print.

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: the active OD/ID finish insert (chamfer is a finish-pass move, no dedicated tool)

optimizations_over_baseline: Standardize the A-angle / G76 chamfer idiom as the default lead-in/out + part-face break (matches ~59% shop convention, R11).
Emit chamfer as part of the finish pass (no extra tool change / air move).
safety_gates: G50 cap if the chamfer rides a G96 finish pass
chamfer direction must not gouge the adjacent face (geometry check)

bore_finish.applies_when: Intentional single clean finish pass to bore size (ARCHER, HPFS bores) — DISTINCT from multi-pass ID_boring LAP; the optimizer must NOT force a LAP where one finish pass is correct.

observed_baseline.strategy: Single G1 Z plunge to depth at finish stock, sometimes hand-coded; TNR comp often absent.

fixed_params.compensation: TNR comp (G41/G42) MANDATORY on a finish bore
fixed_params.spring_pass: optional 1 at size for tight ID tolerance

variable_params.name: bar_overhang_LD
variable_params.rule: L/D <= 4 steel / <= 6 carbide; derate or escalate whiskey

variable_params.name: finish_feed_per_rev
variable_params.rule: Ra = f^2/(8*nose_R); keep >= insert min chip load

variable_params.name: sfm
variable_params.note: G96 CSS preferred where bore dia varies; G50 cap

bore_finish.cutting_condition_rule: single finish pass; feed from required Ra (accuracy-first); SFM physics-delegated, derated by bar deflection; G96 where dia varies (G50 capped).

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: finish boring bar (.015R, shortest reaching depth)

optimizations_over_baseline: Do NOT force a multi-pass LAP where a single finish bore to size is correct (avoids needless air passes).
MANDATORY TNR comp on the finish bore (baseline ~79% omit comp -> ID radius/taper accuracy rides the programmer).
Optional spring pass for tight ID tolerance.
safety_gates: TNR comp mandatory for ID accuracy
chip evac on deep blind bore

live_tool_milling.applies_when: Driven-tool milling/drilling on a turning center: cross-holes, flats, slots, polar/C-axis features (~7% of corpus: M110/G138 polar, M13 SB=, C-axis arcs).

observed_baseline.strategy: M110/G138 polar coordinate, M13 SB=<rpm> rotary-tool spindle, FEED MODE SWITCHES G94 (feed/min) for the milling move then reverts to G95 (feed/rev) for turning. G4 dwell on plunge.
observed_baseline.note: MILLING physics (feed-per-tooth), NOT turning — distinct cutting-condition surface.

fixed_params.spindle: live-tool spindle M13/M14 SB=<rpm>; main spindle C-axis clamp (M110/M15)
fixed_params.feed_mode: G94 (in/min) for the milling move; REVERT to G95 after

variable_params.name: feed_in_per_min
variable_params.rule: G94 in/min — NOT in/rev (live-tool is the one place G94 is correct)

variable_params.name: peck
variable_params.rule: peck deep cross-holes

live_tool_milling.cutting_condition_rule: MILLING conditions (feed-per-tooth -> G94 in/min) from speed_feed milling surface; revert to G95 after; C-axis clamp during milling; rpm = live-tool spindle SB=.

jm_tool_mapping.tool_class: driven endmill / spot+drill in live holder (ER collet)

optimizations_over_baseline: Assert the G94<->G95 feed-mode switch is explicit + reverted (the one place G94 is correct on a lathe) — units-first.
Use milling (feed-per-tooth) physics, not turning, for live-tool moves.
Peck deep cross-holes; C-axis clamp during milling for rigidity.
safety_gates: feed-mode MUST revert to G95 after the milling move (else next turning feed is 12-60x wrong)
C-axis clamp engaged before milling load

peck_drill.applies_when: Deep axial hole on centerline where depth/dia > ~3-5x or gummy material — DISTINCT from shallow drilling_centering (corpus: only ~23-26% peck; many deep holes single-plunged = breakage risk).

observed_baseline.strategy: G74 X0 Z-<depth> D<peck> L<retract> F<feed> peck cycle (when used); too often a single G1 Z-d plunge (ITW Z-3.65, ACME Z-6., AEROTECH 2 in).

fixed_params.cycle: Okuma G74 X0 Z-<depth> D<peck> L<retract> F (peck drill); on G97 direct rpm (axial, no CSS)
fixed_params.coolant: through-spindle or flood; peck for chip clear

variable_params.name: peck_depth
variable_params.rule: peck ~ 1-1.5x dia; scale to dia, not a fixed 0.15in

variable_params.name: rpm
variable_params.rule: rpm = SFM*12/(pi*dia); cap at min(spindle_max, drill_mfr_max)

peck_drill.cutting_condition_rule: G74 peck on G97; peck depth proportional to dia + chip-break need; rpm per-dia capped; feed in/REV.
optimizations_over_baseline: Auto-insert G74 peck when depth/dia > ~3-5x or gummy material (baseline single-plunges deep holes -> chip-pack/drill snap).
Peck depth proportional to dia, not a fixed value (fewer pecks on shallow, longer retract on deep/gummy).
Raise the timid .001-.003 IPR drill feed within rigidity.
safety_gates: rpm capped (small drills snap as rpm explodes with 1/dia)
through-coolant or peck-retract for chip evac
